name: Balch & Bingham

summary.text: Balch & Bingham LLP is a Birmingham, Alabama law firm founded in 1922 by former Alabama Attorney General William Logan Martin Jr., who also served as attorney for Alabama Power Company, a longstanding client. The firm describes itself as having more than 200 attorneys with offices in Alabama, Florida, Georgia, Mississippi, Texas and Washington, D.C., with a focus on regulated industries including energy. In 2018 a federal jury convicted partner Joel Iverson Gilbert, together with Drummond Company vice president David Roberson, of bribing Alabama Representative Oliver Robinson to oppose EPA's Superfund work in North Birmingham; the Eleventh Circuit affirmed the convictions.

sources.title: Federal Jury Convicts Lawyer and Coal Company Executive of Bribing State Legislator

facts.claim: The firm was founded in Birmingham in 1922 by William Logan Martin Jr., who had served as Alabama Attorney General from 1915 to 1917 and as attorney for Alabama Power Company; it operated first as Martin, Thompson & Turner and took the name Balch & Bingham in 1985.

sources.title: Ala. Lawyers Hall of Fame inductees include founder of Balch, former B'ham mayor, dean of legal profession

facts.claim: Alabama Power Company, headed by the founder's brother Tom Martin, was a primary early client; many of the firm's attorneys began in Alabama Power's legal department and some returned to the utility as executives.
facts.quote: A primary client was the Alabama Power Company, which had been headed by Martin's brother, Tom.

facts.claim: The firm describes itself as having more than 200 attorneys across offices in Birmingham and Montgomery, Alabama; Jacksonville, Florida; Atlanta and Augusta, Georgia; Gulfport and Jackson, Mississippi; Houston and Austin, Texas; and Washington, D.C., with experience in regulated industries including energy, financial services and healthcare.

In September 2017 a federal grand jury in the Northern District of Alabama indicted Balch & Bingham partners Joel Iverson Gilbert and Steven George McKinney and Drummond Company vice president David Lynn Roberson on charges of conspiring to bribe state legislator Oliver Robinson; charges against McKinney were later dropped before the case went to the jury.

sources.title: Federal Grand Jury Indicts Two Lawyers and Coal Company VP for Conspiracy to Bribe Legislator
Appeals court confirms bribery convictions of Birmingham lawyer, coal company executive

facts.claim: A federal jury convicted Gilbert and Roberson of bribery, honest services wire fraud, conspiracy and money laundering conspiracy after more than three weeks of testimony before U.S. District Judge Abdul Kallon; prosecutors said the bribe took the form of a consulting contract that paid Robinson $360,000 through the Oliver Robinson Foundation in 2015 and 2016, in exchange for which Robinson lobbied EPA and state officials and voted for a resolution drafted by Gilbert opposing EPA's efforts.
facts.quote: The bribe came in the form of a consulting contract that paid Robinson $360,000 through the Oliver Robinson Foundation, a non-profit organization, between 2015 and 2016.

sources.title: Federal Jury Convicts Lawyer and Coal Company Executive of Bribing State Legislator

facts.claim: Oliver Robinson pleaded guilty in September 2017 to conspiracy, bribery, wire fraud and tax evasion and testified for the prosecution.

sources.title: Federal Jury Convicts Lawyer and Coal Company Executive of Bribing State Legislator

facts.claim: The Eleventh Circuit rejected Gilbert's and Roberson's argument that their conduct did not meet the legal definition of bribery and affirmed their convictions, describing concealed payments of hundreds of thousands of dollars to an Alabama representative through his charitable foundation in exchange for official acts aimed at undermining EPA's cleanup of a Superfund site.
facts.quote: concealed payments of hundreds of thousands of dollars to an Alabama Representative through his charitable foundation

openQuestions: Site claim that a Drummond vice president and a Balch & Bingham partner were convicted of bribing Oliver Robinson to oppose an EPA Superfund cleanup, that Robinson pleaded guilty, and that the convictions were upheld on appeal is supported by the three DOJ press releases.
Site description of the neighbourhood as 'mostly Black' is not addressed in the DOJ releases opened; the owner may want a source for the demographic description.
The year of the Eleventh Circuit decision (May 27) was not given in the sources opened; the DOJ release should carry the date.
Whether Drummond was a client of Balch & Bingham in the Superfund matter is not stated in the DOJ releases; the firm's current relationship with Alabama Power or Southern Company was not confirmed.
